title: Attended Polysomnography and Home Sleep Apnea Testing

criteria.summary: Home sleep apnea test nondiagnostic, negative despite high suspicion, or contraindicated

passages.text: This policy applies to outpatient professional claims for attended in-laboratory polysomnography, CPT 95810, and unattended home sleep apnea testing, CPT 95806, with dates of service on or after January 1, 2026.
Home sleep apnea testing is considered medically necessary when criterion 3.1 is met. Attended polysomnography is considered medically necessary when criteria 3.1 and 3.2 are both met.
The member has symptoms of obstructive sleep apnea: habitual snoring or witnessed apneas, together with excessive daytime sleepiness, for example an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score above 10.

A home sleep apnea test was nondiagnostic, or was negative despite a high pretest probability, or is contraindicated by a documented comorbidity: moderate or severe cardiopulmonary disease, neuromuscular disease, or chronic opioid use.

Documentation supporting each applicable criterion must be available in the medical record on request. Absence of documentation for a required criterion does not establish that the criterion was not met.
